idiom_name: state hoisting (remember/mutableStateOf or ViewModel) + stateless @Composable child
implementation_notes: Compose documents the split as the best practice: hoist UI state to the lowest common ancestor of the composables that read and write it, keep it closest to where it is consumed, and expose immutable state plus events from the owner. The stateful wrapper composable - or a ViewModel collected with collectAsStateWithLifecycle - is the container, and the child takes value plus onValueChange. Because state is external to a composable by design, the stateless child is the default and a wrapper is the deliberate exception; complex UI logic belongs in a plain state holder or the ViewModel rather than in the composable.
pitfalls: Building a stateful composable and hoisting later duplicates state and breaks previews and tests; start stateless unless one composable is the only reader.
`remember { derive(param) }` freezes a value computed from a parameter on first composition - use remember(param) or derivedStateOf for recomputation.

Screen-scoped state holders should not be reused for reusable UI components: the same ViewModel instance is then shared across every usage under the same owner, so use the component's own state holder instead.

variants.name: Classic View system with a ViewModel state holder
variants.idiom_name: Activity/Fragment as container + ViewModel exposing StateFlow, XML views passive
variants.implementation_notes: Before Compose the container was an Activity or Fragment: it observes the state a ViewModel exposes and pushes values into XML-defined views, while those views stay passive - they receive text, visibility and listeners and never reach for the repository themselves. The ViewModel's documented job is to persist UI state across configuration changes and to hold the business logic the UI layer needs, which is exactly the state-owner role; keep it unaware of view types and never pass it down into reusable child components.
pitfalls: Collecting a StateFlow without the lifecycle owner keeps updating views after the view is destroyed; use repeatOnLifecycle or flowWithLifecycle.
ViewModels must not hold Context, View or Resource references - they outlive the view and leak it; expose state and let the container translate it.
Adapter row views that cache mutable state break the stateless-child rule once rows are recycled; bind everything from the current item.
